title: The Wisdom of Happiness, film screening and panel discussion featuring Richard Gere, executive producer
description:
Join Student Affairs and Campus Life, the Fine Arts Center and the International Campaign for Tibet for this free film screening and panel discussion featuring actor and UMass alumnus Richard Gere.

 

Admission is free, but space is limited, and advance registration is strongly recommended.

 

Gere is one of the executive producers of the 2024 documentary film Wisdom of Happiness, which offers an intimate and inspiring portrait of the fourteenth Dalai Lama, one of the world’s most influential spiritual leaders and a Nobel Peace Prize laureate.

 

Through personal reflections and conversations, Wisdom of Happiness explores compassion as a practical response to today's greatest challenges — from conflict and loneliness to climate change and social division. The film invites audiences to see compassion not as an abstract ideal, but a way of living that can transform individuals, communities, and society. WIth its message of hope, resilience, and shared humanity, Wisdom of Happiness speaks to people of many backgrounds and beliefs.

 

A post-screening panel discussion moderated by Monte Belmonte of New England Public Media’s The Fabulous 413 will include Gere, US Representative Jim McGovern, and Tencho Gyatso, president of the International Campaign for Tibet. Dhardon Sharling, lecturer of communication, UMass Amherst will serve as emcee for the evening.

 

This event is presented with support from the Fine Arts Center's Education and Engagement department and Asian and Asian American Arts and Cultures Program.

title: "Solutions Through Empowerment: Why Health and Education Matter to Climate Change," Special Zube Webinar Presented by Hannah Evans
description:
The fall semester of Zube Lectures kicks off with "Solutions Through Empowerment: Why Health and Education Matter to Climate Change," a special, one-time-only, virtual talk presented by Hannah Evans, Senior Analyst of Outreach and Global Partnerships at Population Connection. The webinar will be held on Zoom on Thursday, September 10th, at 4:00 p.m.

 

This virtual talk is free and open to the public. No registration required.

 

Zoom Webinar Link: https://umass-amherst.zoom.us/j/91851697293

 

About the Talk

Worldwide, population pressures contribute to immediate dangers like food insecurity, natural resource scarcity, inequality, and climate-changing emissions. Yet, the relationship between population and climate change is complex. Although the carbon footprints of most of the world’s population are negligible relative to that of the average American or European, low- and middle-income countries are disproportionately vulnerable to climate impacts like rising sea-levels and extreme weather events. Additionally, the close relationship between high fertility and poverty throughout the world worsens climate vulnerability and puts more people at risk. This presentation uses a climate justice framework to explore the ways in which demographic trends impact and are impacted by climate change and argues that gender equality must be better integrated into global climate solutions. The talk will conclude with a discussion on the ways in which expanding access to health care and education—especially for women, girls, and reproductively capable people—act as necessary building blocks for climate adaptation and resilience across the globe.

 

About the Speaker

Hannah Evans is interested in working with students, professors, and activists to promote positive social and environmental change. Her work investigates the ways in population dynamics intersect with global social, political, economic, and environmental systems and advocates for integrated developmental solutions that simultaneously combat climate change and societal injustices. She develops and gives comprehensive, solution-oriented presentations focused on the connections between global population growth, access to health care and education, women’s empowerment, and climate adaptation.

 Through an examination of some of the root causes of high fertility, Evans' work seeks to highlight the interconnections between poverty, resource use and consumption, population pressures, women’s rights, and environmental challenges made worse by climate change. At Population Connection, she focuses on public speaking and the development of open-source, academic-style resources. She also cultivates partnerships between Population Connection and international NGOs. Before joining Population Connection’s staff, Evans worked as an adjunct professor of Women’s Studies and taught classes on gender, science, and feminist theory. She has non-profit experience working as a program developer for sustainable agriculture and public health programs in Honduras and Panama and has worked as a researcher studying food security issues throughout Southern California. 

Evans holds a BA in Environmental Policy and Natural Resource Conservation and Political Science and a Master’s in Political Ecology from San Diego State University, where her research focused on sustainability labeling and ethical consumption between the United States and Nicaragua.

title: Nocturnal Insect Night Walk
description:
Crickets and katydids are a hallmark of the summer night, and their enchanting songs are known to many… but did you know that we have nearly 70 species of them in Massachusetts alone, each with a distinct, identifiable call? Join the UMass Bee Campus Committee and Fernald Club for a stroll on Nocturnal Insect Night, and discover how the summer night comes alive! Watch colorful katydids and crickets emerge from the undergrowth to sing together in a great chorus, while daytime pollinators snuggle into flowers to wait out the night.

 

Meet at the front of Fernald Hall. The walk will be about a mile in length, and you can find our intended path here. We will be taking several stops along the way.


RSVP HERE: https://forms.gle/LfcS6FTHf8agwmFA8

 

What to bring: Water, snacks, a flashlight and comfortable clothes you don't mind getting dirty.

 

Download iNaturalist: Please download the iNaturalist app ahead of time if possible! Here is the link for iPhone and here is the link for Android. We will introduce how to use iNaturalist at the beginning of the event!

 

Accessibility: This will be an outdoor event on a mix of paved paths and grass with uneven terrain. Benches are available throughout the walk and restrooms are located in nearby campus buildings. Masks are not required at this event (and are welcome!). Please be mindful of your own and group safety. If you or anyone in your household are not feeling well, please do not attend this event. Please let us know if there is anything we can do to accommodate you at this event by reaching out to abolesfassle@umass.edu or @bjyoo@umass.edu.

 

Note: if you are registering for family members or multiple people please just let us know how many folks you are RSVPing for in the comments section, thanks!

title: Better Tech: Putting People First in Cyberspace with Francine Berman and Jim Kurose
description:
On the publication day of “Better Tech: Putting People First in Cyberspace,” Francine Berman will join Jim Kurose for a timely conversation about how technology can better serve - and protect - the people who depend on it. 
 
From social media and AI chatbots to search engines, some of today's most essential technologies also carry significant risks. In “Better Tech”, Berman asks what would change if we treated cyberspace as critical infrastructure: something the public should be able to expect will be safe, dependable, and trustworthy. The book moves beyond diagnosing the problem to offer practical strategies for responsible design, development, use, and governance.

 

Francine Berman is co-founder and director of Public Interest Technology and the Stuart Rice Honorary Research Professor in the Manning College of Information and Computer Sciences at UMass Amherst, as well as Faculty Associate in the Berkman Klein Center for Internet and Society at Harvard. A distinguished data scientist and computing leader, her work focuses on the impact of information technology on society and strategies that help minimize public risk and maximize public benefits. Berman is the inaugural recipient of the ACM/IEEE Ken Kennedy Award, the 2020 Paul Evan Peters Award, and the 2024 NCWIT Pioneer in Tech Award. She is former head of the San Diego Supercomputer Center and an elected member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. 

 

Jim Kurose is Distinguished University Professor Emeritus of computer science at UMass Amherst. Internationally recognized for his work in computer networking, he has held leadership roles at UMass Amherst and the National Science Foundation, where he led the Directorate for Computer and Information Science and Engineering. Kurose is a member of the National Academy of Engineering and co-author of Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach. 

 

The conversation begins at 4:00 p.m. on Tuesday, September 15, at the UMass Amherst Old Chapel. A book signing will follow the conversation, with a limited number of complimentary copies of “Better Tech” available to the first registered attendees.  
 
Registration is recommended for in-person attendees and is required to receive the livestream link.

title: Design for Learning: Four Principles for Better Slides, Pages, and Print
description:
Poor design can undermine even the most thought-provoking courses, leaving students distracted and less engaged. In this interactive, hands-on workshop, you will learn four simple design principles—contrast, repetition, alignment, and proximity—that can instantly make your content more organized, polished, and engaging.

 

This workshop will address the following questions:

How can contrast, repetition, alignment, and proximity elevate the clarity and impact of visual communication?What common design mistakes can unintentionally distract or confuse students?How can these principles be applied across a range of instructional resources? 

We will use Zoom Whiteboards to reflect on sample designs to see the principles in action. By the end of the workshop, you will leave with practical design strategies that you can apply to a range of visual materials, including Canvas pages, slide decks, handouts, and flyers.

 

This is the first workshop in the Design for Learning series running this semester.

title: Find Your Way: Map, Compass, and Natural Navigation
description:
Find Your Way: Map, Compass, and Natural Navigation with RecWell Adventure Programs Ages 18–90. Waivers required. Prerequisite for Chart a Course.

 

Paper maps and compasses work when phones fail. This two-hour workshop is split between the classroom and the field, covering foundational navigation skills-and the judgment to use them well-that hold up in any conditions.

 

You'll learn to read a topographic map, take and follow a bearing, adjust for declination, and calculate your personal pace count over real terrain. The field portion puts each skill into practice sequentially. You'll also cover triangulation for confirming position, essential orienteering vocabulary, and natural navigation cues (sun, stars, tree growth, prevailing wind) for backup awareness, not as a party trick.

 

Groups stay together throughout. No prior experience needed. This workshop is the prerequisite for Chart a Course, RecWell's team orienteering challenge.

 

Dress for the outdoors. All equipment provided.

title: Stand-Up Paddleboarding Basics
description:
Curious about stand-up paddleboarding? Join us for a fun, beginner-friendly introduction that will have you confidently paddling in no time. This two-hour session begins in the pool and progresses to open water, covering everything from reading conditions and rigging your board to finding your balance, falling safely, and getting back on.

 

You'll learn essential paddling strokes, practice self-rescue skills before heading onto open water, and finish with unstructured paddle time to build confidence and put your new skills into practice.

 

With small groups on the water, you'll receive plenty of individualized instruction and feedback throughout the session. No experience is necessary, just bring a willingness to get wet!

 

What to bring: Swimwear or quick-dry clothing. All paddling equipment is provided.

description:
A well-designed Canvas homepage is more than just a landing page, it is a launchpad for student learning. In this hands-on workshop, participants will explore how thoughtful homepage design can enhance navigation, set clear expectations, and foster student engagement. Through practical examples and guided activities, attendees will learn how to structure their Canvas homepage to support diverse learners and improve course clarity.

How to structure Canvas Homepage to promote clarity, engagement, and easy navigation?In what ways can Canvas tools (like buttons, images, and links) enhance homepage usability?What are common design pitfalls in Canvas Homepages and how can we avoid them?

title: Insun Park & Generals
description:
We’re just going to say it: You have to see this band. Their live shows are A-MAZ-ING!

 

South Korea’s Insun Park & Generals deliver a visually entrancing, musically engrossing stage show that will lift your spirits and leave you buzzing for weeks.

 

The band blends Korean traditional music with a mix of contemporary pop forms — notably rock, funk, and hip-hop — to create a unique sound that is expansive and inescapably danceable. And bandleader Park infuses movement and storytelling into the live experience through her mastery of Gangnyeong Talchum, a centuries old mask dance designated as part of Korea’s national intangible heritage. Park stands out as one of the few female masters of an art form historically dominated by men.

 

Simultaneously preserving tradition and shaping the future of Korean performing arts, Insun Park & Generals come off as cultural ambassadors with a kick. Be sure to join us for this transformative experience.

title: Christian McBride and Ursa Major
description:
Christian McBride, bass; Nicole Glover, saxophone; Ely Perlman, guitar; Mike King, piano; Savannah Harris, drums

 

Christian McBride’s 2026 started with a flourish. In February, he picked up his tenth and eleventh Grammy Awards, with the honors coming in a manner that neatly illustrates the scope of McBride’s career as a bassist, bandleader, and composer. There was the Best Large Jazz Ensemble Album award that went to the Christian McBride Big Band’s Without Further Ado, Vol 1. And there was his piece of the Best Jazz Performance award for “Windows (Live)” one of many remarkable tracks on the album Trilogy 3, a release drawn from piano legend Chick Corea’s final trio tour. McBride also shares with the late Corea and drummer Brian Blade a pair of Best Instrumental Jazz Album Grammys for Trilogy and Trilogy 2.

 

McBride’s career Grammy wins are split between his work as a bandleader/composer and his work as a sideman. And that only makes sense. McBride, who started playing professionally at age seventeen, has spent thirty-seven years moving fluidly between the roles of bandleader and band member. He’s released nineteen albums as a leader, been part of six collaborative albums, and appeared as a sideman on more than 400 releases. And because that somehow hasn’t kept him busy enough, McBride also served as artistic director of the Newport Jazz Festival from 2015 to 2025, hosts NPR’s Jazz Night In America, and works alongside his wife, Melissa Walker, as a jazz educator.

 

Ursa Major ties many of the threads of McBride’s career together. Formed in 2022, the band places McBride in the company of four rising star musicians. And though firmly grounded in jazz, the band’s music works in elements of R&B, soul, funk, and disco. This is McBride picking up where the late Corea left off, reimagining jazz fusion and in bringing together and mentoring extraordinarily talented, innovative musicians whose futures as players and bandleaders are wide open. Best of all, when this ensemble takes the stage, it plays with a combination of energy and mastery that is as joyful as it is jaw-dropping.

title: Artist Talk: Dianne Smith
description:
In her exhibition Sonic Futures, Radiant Bodies, artist Dianne Smith envisions Black futurity through photography, sound, performance, sculpture, and ritual. Hear directly from Smith and insight into her exhibition and artistic process.

About Dianne Smith

Dianne Smith is a Bronx-born multidisciplinary artist of Belizean descent whose artistic career spans decades. Her work has been featured in numerous solo and group exhibitions addressing a range of themes and mediums, including her solo exhibition Two Turntables and a Microphone at The Bronx Museum, which celebrated fifty years of hip-hop. She was one of three artists with solo presentations in Visions for Our Future, Echoes of Our Past at the Institute of Contemporary Art at Maine College of Art & Design, and her work has been included in The Way We Remember and the Uptown Triennial at the Wallach Art Gallery, Columbia University.

Smith received the Nancy Graves Foundation Award and a Fulbright from the United States Consulate General in Guayaquil, Ecuador. Her work is included in collections including the National Museum of Women in the Arts, The Bronx Museum, the Brodsky Organization, and the Petrucci Family Foundation Collection of African American Art. She lives and works in Harlem, New York.

title: Sugar Skull! A Día de Muertos Musical Adventure!
description:
Keep the family fun of spooky season going for an extra week with this special matinee event! Sugar Skull! A Día de Muertos Musical Adventure is a bilingual/bicultural musical for young audiences and families that uses traditional regional music and dance from Mexico to tell the story of twelve-year-old Vita Flores. Vita thinks her family has gone loco planning a celebration for deceased loved ones. Why throw a party for the dead? But when a spirited candy skeleton suddenly springs to life, Vita finds herself on a magical, musical journey to unravel the true meaning of Día de Muertos.

 

With her skeletal new friend, Vita dances with ancient ancestors, sings with a sorrowful sorceress, escapes the trickster chaneques, and even meets the famous Catrina Calavera. But can this clever youth gather the missing pieces needed for her family ofrenda before it’s too late?

 

Family pack: 25% off of up to two adult tickets with the purchase of at least one youth ticket
